summary: Czechia is part of the EU and the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities can stay 90 days in any 180-day period (with the ETIAS travel authorisation being phased in), and everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa costing €90.

fee.notes: Children 6–11: €45; under 6: free. Fee set EU-wide since 11 June 2024.
For stays over 90 days: work, study, family, business and other long-stay purposes. Some categories are reduced or exempt.
For courses longer than 90 days; needs proof of enrolment at a Czech institution, accommodation, funds and health insurance. Some study categories are fee-exempt.
Combined work and residence permit for employment over 90 days; requires a job listed in the central vacancy register and an employer in Czechia.

passportValidity.text: Non-EU passports must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure from the Schengen Area and have been issued within the last 10 years.

travelInsurance.text: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. Visa-exempt visitors are not required to show it but border officers may ask about cover.

onwardTicket.text: Border officers may ask non-EU visitors for proof of return or onward travel and accommodation details.

proofOfFunds.text: Non-EU visitors may be asked to show sufficient funds for their stay. The amount is derived from the Czech subsistence minimum and depends on the length of stay — in practice a bank card with a reasonable balance or the equivalent in cash is accepted.

declarations.name: EES — Entry/Exit System (biometric registration)
declarations.submitWindow: At the border on first entry
declarations.text: Non-EU travellers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Registration happens at the border — there is nothing to submit in advance, but allow extra time on your first entry.

declarations.name: ETIAS — European Travel Information and Authorisation System

fee.notes: Free for under-18s and over-70s. Valid 3 years or until passport expiry.

declarations.text: Visa-exempt travellers will need an ETIAS travel authorisation to enter the Schengen Area. It is being phased in — check the official EU site for the current status and apply only there.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of €10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared when entering or leaving the EU.

notes: Duty-free from outside the EU: 200 cigarettes, 1 litre of spirits, goods up to €300 (€430 arriving by air/sea).
No limits on goods for personal use when arriving from another EU country.

payments.text: Cards and contactless payments are accepted almost everywhere, including small purchases. Czechia does not use the euro — pay in koruna and avoid street currency exchanges.

safety.text: Czechia is one of Europe's safest destinations. The main risks for visitors are pickpocketing in central Prague, taxi overcharging and rigged currency exchanges.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Czechia Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: April–June and September–October offer mild weather and thinner crowds in Prague; December is popular for Christmas markets, July–August is peak season.

tips.text: The 90-day limit counts across the entire Schengen Area, not just Czechia — days spent in Germany or Austria count against the same allowance.

Never use street currency exchanges or money changers offering 'zero commission' in central Prague — many pay rates 20–30% below market. Withdraw koruna from bank ATMs (declining conversion) or use cards.
Hailing taxis on the street in Prague risks heavy overcharging — use apps (Uber, Bolt, Liftago) or ask your hotel to call a reputable company.
First-time EES biometric registration can add queue time at airports — arrive with margin on your first Schengen entry.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Czechia?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can visit Czechia and the rest of the Schengen Area visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS becomes mandatory, they will need to obtain this online authorisation (€20) before travel.

faq.question: How much does a Czech Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11. It allows stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries, and applications are decided within 15–45 calendar days.

faq.question: Does Czechia use the euro?
faq.answer: No. Czechia uses the Czech koruna (CZK). Cards are accepted almost everywhere; if you need cash, withdraw from bank ATMs and decline dynamic currency conversion — never use street exchange offices in Prague, which offer very poor rates.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Czechia?
faq.answer: ETIAS is being phased in for visa-exempt travellers. During the transition period travellers without ETIAS are still admitted; once fully mandatory, the €20 online authorisation will be required before boarding. Check the official EU website for the current status.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Czechia without a visa?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt non-EU visitors can stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area. EU and EFTA citizens can stay indefinitely but must register locally after 3 months.
